newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares slip on petroleum price hike prospect.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares slip on petroleum price hike prospect.

text.p: Prospects of an imminent increase in petroleum products' prices triggered selling on the Delhi Stock Exchange, driving share prices lower in afternoon trade on Monday, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index was 12.73 points lower at 777.81 points at 12:45 p.m. (0715 GMT).
"Most of the major players have been on a selling spree after it became clear that the government would soon increase the price of petroleum products," said one broker.
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said last week he could not avoid raising the prices of petroleum products.

In an interview on state-run Doordarshan television, Gujral called for public support in tackling the oil pool deficit, pegged at 155 billion rupees ($4.32 billion) at the end of 1996/97 (April-March).
The oil pool deficit is the subsidy the federal government owes to state-run oil companies for selling their products well below international prices.
Reliance Industries fell 3.50 rupees to 301.00 on speculative selling, brokers said.
